text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today as oil prices dipped slightly—US crude dropped to $91.48 per barrel—and the stock gave back some of the sharp gains it posted over the past four trading days (up nearly 5% from August 28 to September 2). The pullback appears modest and technical after a strong run, rather than driven by any fresh negative news about the company itself.

The broader backdrop remains supportive for oil majors: diesel prices have hit record highs due to refinery disruptions from the Ukraine-Russia conflict, and geopolitical tensions—including EU sanctions on Iran and ongoing efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz—continue to tighten global supply. A potential U.S.-backed deal to increase Venezuelan oil production could eventually add supply, but that remains a longer-term factor and hasn't offset near-term supply tightness.
